newsitem.title: USA: Motorola shares off on Ericsson pricing comment.
newsitem.headline: Motorola shares off on Ericsson pricing comment.

text.p: Shares of Motorola Inc declined three to 64-1/2 after Swedish telecommunications competitor AB LM Ericsson projected continued pricing pressure on telecommunications products in 1997, market sources said.

Earlier, Ericsson said it saw signs of similar price pressures on all products in 1997 as it experienced in 1996. Ericsson said that price pressures on its products in 1996 were about in line with its forecasts, except for mobile telephones, which were somewhat less than expected.

Market sources said the Heard on the Street Column in Tuesday's Wall Street Journal also pressured Motorola's stock. The column said Motorola faces challenges in its markets, including cellular telephones.
The column also reported that Motorola sought assurances that it would receive payment of a $35 million bill in the bankruptcy court case of MobileMedia, a big paging customer.

"Today's Heard on the Street article was critical of Motorola's sound business practices of dealing aggressively with marginal distributors," Gruntal analyst Mona Eraiba said in a report. "...Accordingly, supporting a marginal paging service supplier in trouble goes beyond Motorola's common business practices. Moreover, it is not healthy for the pager market in the long term."

Eraiba, who rates Motorola a strong buy and recommends purchase of shares with an $80 a share price target, said Motorola holds 38 percent of the cellular subscriber market worldwide. That market is expected to grow by more than 50 percent in 1997.
"Motorola's new revamped product line is meeting with enthusiastic demand," Eraiba said.
